title: ASEAN Summit Day 3: Trump's late arrival, handover to Singapore

blocks.text: November 17, 2026 | 9:26pm
US President Donald Trump gestures upon arriving at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport to attend the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit in Manila on November 17, 2026.
AFP / Eloisa Lopez / Pool

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines handed the ASEAN chairship to Singapore on Tuesday, November 17 as the bloc's 49th summit closed in Manila, with leaders acting on more than 100 outcome documents but leaving a long-stalled South China Sea code of conduct unfinished.
Leaders stayed in the capital for an evening "special" summit with United States President Donald Trump, who arrived late Tuesday afternoon.
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. called it "a very informal kind of summit," though he said it would produce outcome documents.

Trump is also set to hold talks with Marcos before flying to China for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meeting, where he is to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

At a news briefing — where he took no free-wheeling questions to rush for the bloc's summit with Trump — Marcos said negotiations on the sea code were 85 to 90 percent complete, with only definitions of terms left to settle.
Foreign Affairs Secretary Theresa Lazaro said Sunday that three of four "milestone" issues remained open, including whether the code would be legally binding.
Looking back at the past year, Marcos said leaders had "navigated a very, very, very difficult year," with crises that "there was no way to anticipate."
Manila's year as chair coincided with the war in the Middle East, which pushed up fuel prices across the region, and with continuing confrontations with China at sea.
Protesters angry with the economic fallout of the US-Iran war and the US-led Pax Silica initiative clashed with police in Manila on Sunday at the opening of the summit.

On the final day of the summit, Marcos chaired the 29th ASEAN Plus Three summit with China, Japan and South Korea, and the 21st East Asia Summit, which also includes the United States, Russia, India, Australia and New Zealand.
Plus Three leaders adopted a statement on maritime trade and logistics connectivity and on energy and food security amid supply shocks.
Marcos said the Middle East war "certainly accelerated the process," pointing to Philippine and Japanese proposals to stockpile energy.
East Asia Summit leaders also adopted a declaration on regional stability and a statement pledging closer law-enforcement cooperation and information sharing against online scams.

On Myanmar, leaders agreed to keep the military-backed government's leaders barred from top-level meetings, but said they could gradually restore its full political representation if it makes "sustained and concrete" progress on ASEAN's five-point peace plan.
"The ball is very much now in the court of Myanmar and its present leadership," Marcos said.

Marcos also cited the conclusion of the ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement, which he called the world's first region-wide pact of its kind. It is meant to ease cross-border e-commerce and set common rules on data and digital payments. He said ASEAN should not just be "customers to the AI revolution" led by China and the United States.
Other outcomes included a memorandum to advance a regional power grid and a disaster-response framework that formalizes aid Marcos said member states had previously given informally.
He said the first undersea cable for cross-border power sharing would be laid between Sabah in Malaysia and Mindanao.
As well, Cyprus, Slovakia and Slovenia acceded to ASEAN's Treaty of Amity and Cooperation, bringing its parties to 65.
